page.overview:
What is Defense Against the Dark Arts?

Defence Against the Dark Arts (abbreviated as DADA) was a subject and core class taught at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry and Ilvermorny School of Witchcraft and Wizardry curses, hexes and jinxes (dark charms), and duelling.

At some point before the start of the First Wizarding War in 1970, Tom Riddle applied to the position of Defence Against the Dark Arts professor, but Albus Dumbledore rejected him. Riddle never had any actual intention of becoming a teacher, he only returned to the school so he could hide the diadem Horcrux in a place he believed no one else knew about, but the rejection infuriated him all the same, so he jinxed the post of Defence Professor so that no one could hold the office for more than a single school year. The circumstances of their departure were always different, but they no longer taught it all the same, and as such, the subject had numerous Professors over the years, some were good, others were lousy. When Voldemort was finally defeated once and for all in the Battle of Hogwarts in 1998, the curse was broken.

Ilvermorny began teaching the subject in the 17th century.

Defence Against the Dark Arts was a required subject from first year to fifth year. Inadequate teachers, such as Quirinus Quirrell and Dolores Umbridge, who were focused on theories alone, hampered the learning of defences, as they would not be providing students any practical experiences.
